items.head: 33 CFR 165.901 Great Lakes—regulated navigation areas and safety zones
items.place: Great Lakes—regulated navigation areas and safety zones
items.quote: (a) The following are regulated navigation areas:  Lake Huron. (i) The waters of Lake Huron known as South Channel between Bois Blanc Island and Cheboygan, Michigan; bounded by a line north from Cheboygan Crib Light at 45°39′48″N., 84°27′36″W.; to Bois Blanc Island at 45°43′42″N., 84°27′36″W.; and a line north from the mainland at 45°43′00″N., 84°35′30″W; to the western tangent of Bois Blanc Island at 45°48′42″N., 84°35′30″W.

items.head: 33 CFR 165.902 Safety Zone; Lower Niagara River at Niagara Falls, New York
items.place: Lower Niagara River at Niagara Falls, New York
items.quote: (a) The following is a safety zone—The United States waters of the Niagara River from the crest of the American and Horseshoe Falls, Niagara Falls, New York to a line drawn across the Niagara River from the downstream side of the mouth of Gill Creek to the upstream end of the breakwater at the mouth of the Welland River.

items.head: 33 CFR 165.903 Safety Zones: Cuyahoga River and Old River, Cleveland OH
items.place: Cuyahoga River and Old River, Cleveland OH
items.quote: The waters of the Cuyahoga River and the Old River extending ten feet into the river at the following eleven locations, including the adjacent shorelines, are safety zones, coordinates for which are based on NAD 83. From the point where the shoreline intersects longitude 81°42'24.5"W., which is the southern side of the Norfolk and Southern railroad bridge, southeasterly along the shore for six hundred feet to the point where the shoreline intersects longitude 81°42'24.5"W., which is the Holy Moses Water Taxi Landing at Fado's Restaurant.

items.head: 33 CFR 165.904 Lake Michigan at Chicago Harbor and Burnham Park Harbor—Safety and Security Zone
items.place: Lake Michigan at Chicago Harbor and Burnham Park Harbor—Safety and Security Zone
items.quote: All waters of Lake Michigan within Burnham Park Harbor shoreward of a line across the entrance of the harbor connecting coordinates 41°51'09"N., 087°36'36"W. and 41°51'11"N., 087°36'22"W. (b) Effective times and dates . This safety and security zone will be in effect at various times to be published in the Coast Guard Local Notice to Mariners or broadcasted via Marine Radio VHF-FM Channels 16 and 22.

items.head: 33 CFR 165.906 Lakeside Yacht Club in Cleveland Harbor, Cleveland, OH—regulated navigation areas
items.place: Lakeside Yacht Club in Cleveland Harbor, Cleveland, OH—regulated navigation areas
items.quote: The following are areas inside Cleveland Harbor which are subject to navigational restrictions based on the height of vessel masts as specified in paragraph (b) of this section. For the purpose of this section, the term “mast” will be used to include masts, antennae or any other portion of the vessel extending above the waterline.

items.head: 33 CFR 165.910 Security Zones; Captain of the Port Lake Michigan
items.place: Captain of the Port Lake Michigan
items.quote: The following areas, defined by coordinates based upon North American Datum 1983, are security zones:  Jardine Water Filtration Plant —(i) Location. All waters of Lake Michigan within the arc of a 100- yard radius with its center located on the north wall of Jardine Water Filtration Plant, approximate position 41°53'46"N., 087°36'23"W.; (NAD 83).

items.head: 33 CFR 165.911 Security Zones; Captain of the Port Eastern Great Lakes Zone
items.place: Captain of the Port Eastern Great Lakes Zone
items.quote: The following are security zones:  Nine Mile Point and Fitzpatrick Nuclear Power Plants . The navigable waters of Lake America bounded by the following coordinates: commencing at 43°30.8'N., 76°25.7'W.; then north to 43°31.2'N., 76°25.7'W.; then east-northeast to 43°31.6'N., 76°24.9'W.; then east to 43°31.8'N., 76°23.2'W.; then south to 43°31.5'N., 76°23.2'W.; and then following the shoreline back to the point of origin (NAD 83).

items.head: 33 CFR 165.912 Security Zone; Lake Erie, Perry, OH
items.quote: (a) Location : The following area is a security zone: all navigable waters of Lake Erie bounded by a line drawn between the following coordinates beginning at 41° 48.187'N, 081° 08.818'W; then due north to 41° 48.7'N, 081° 08.818'W; then due east to 41° 48.7'N, 081° 08.455'W; then due south to the south shore of Lake Erie at 41° 48.231'N, 081° 08.455'W; thence westerly following the shoreline back to the beginning (NAD 83).

items.head: 33 CFR 165.913 Security Zone; Burke Lakefront Airport, Lake Erie, Cleveland, OH
items.place: Burke Lakefront Airport, Lake Erie, Cleveland, OH
items.quote: This security zone includes all waters extending from the surface to the sea floor within approximately 650 yards seaward from the shoreline of the Burke Lakefront Airport and encompasses all waters in Lake Erie within a line connecting the following geographical positions: 41°31′45″N., 081°39′20″W.; then extending northwest to 41°32′23″N., 081°39′46″W.; then extending southwest to 41°31′02″ N, 081°42′10″ W; then extending southwest to the shoreline at 41°30′38″N., 081°41′53″W., (NAD 83); then following the shoreline back to the point of origin.

items.head: 33 CFR 165.915 Security zones; Captain of the Port Detroit
items.quote: The following areas are security zones:  Enrico Fermi 2 Nuclear Power Station . All waters and adjacent shoreline encompassed by a line commencing at 41°58.4'N., 083°15.4'W.; then northeast to 41°58.5'N., 083°15.0'W.; then southeast to 41°58.2'N., 083°13.7'W.; then south to 41°56.9'N., 083°13.8'W.; then west to 41°56.9'N., 083°15.2'W.; then back to the starting point at 41°58.4'N., 083°15.4'W.

items.head: 33 CFR 165.916 Security Zones; Captain of the Port Milwaukee Zone, Lake Michigan
items.place: Captain of the Port Milwaukee Zone, Lake Michigan
items.quote: The following are security zones:  Kewaunee Nuclear Power Plant . All navigable waters of Western Lake Michigan encompassed by a line commencing from a point on the shoreline at 44°20.715'N., 087°32.080'W., then easterly to 44°20.720'N., 087°31.630'W., then southerly to 44°20.480'N., 087°31.630'W., then westerly to 44°20.480'N., 087°31.970'W., then northerly following the shoreline back to the point of origin (NAD 83).

items.head: 33 CFR 165.920 Regulated Navigation Area: USCG Station Port Huron, MI, Lake Huron
items.place: USCG Station Port Huron, MI, Lake Huron
items.quote: All waters of Lake Huron encompassed by the following: starting at the northwest corner at 43°00.4'N., 082°25.327'W.; then east to 43°00.4'N., 082°25.238'W.; then south to 43°00.3'N., 082°25.238'W.; then west to 43°00.3'N., 082°25.327'W.; then following the shoreline north back to the point of origin (NAD 83).

items.head: 33 CFR 165.927 Safety Zone; St. Louis River, Duluth/Interlake Tar Remediation Site, Duluth, MN
items.place: St. Louis River, Duluth/Interlake Tar Remediation Site, Duluth, MN
items.quote: (a) Location : The following area is a safety zone: All waters of Stryker Bay and Hallett Slips 6 and 7 which are located north of a boundary line delineated by the following points: From the shoreline at 46°43'10.00"N., 092°10'31.66"W, then south to 46°43'06.24"N., 092°10'31.66"W, then east to 46°43'06.24"N., 092°09'41.76"W, then north to the shoreline at 46°43'10.04"N., 092°09'41.76"W. [Datum NAD 83].

items.head: 33 CFR 165.931 Safety Zone; Chicago Harbor, Navy Pier Southeast, Chicago, IL
items.place: Chicago Harbor, Navy Pier Southeast, Chicago, IL
items.quote: The following area is a safety zone: The waters of Lake Michigan within Chicago Harbor bounded by coordinates beginning at 41°53′23.3”N, 087°36′04.5”W; then south to 41°53′11.8”N, 087°36′04.1”W; then east to 41°53′12.1”N, 087°35′40.5”W; then north to 41°53′23.6”N, 087°35′40.07”W; then west back to the point of origin (NAD 83).

items.head: 33 CFR 334.845 Wisconsin Air National Guard, Volk Field military exercise area located in Lake Michigan offshore from Manitowoc and Sheboygan Counties; Danger Zone
items.quote: The waters within an area beginning at a point at 43°19'00"N., 87°41'00"W.; to 44°05'30"N., 87°29'45"W.; to 44°02'00"N., 87°02'30"W.; to 43°15'30"N., 87°14'00"W.; thence to the point of beginning. (b) The regulation . During specific, infrequent periods when Military exercises will be conducted, as promulgated in the Local Notice to mariners published by the United States Coast Guard (USCG), all vessels entering the danger zone are advised to proceed across the area by the most direct route and without unnecessary delay.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: The waters of the St. Lawrence River described in this chapter are Great Lakes designated waters. All registered vessels of the United States and foreign vessels are required to have in their service a United States or Canadian registered pilot.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Consult Local Notice to Mariners for additional information and firing schedules.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: The waters of Lake America are Great Lakes undesignated waters; registered vessels of the United States and foreign vessels are required to have in their service a United States or Canadian registered pilot or other officer qualified for Great Lakes undesignated waters. The Welland Canal and its approaches are Great Lakes designated waters; registered vessels of the United States and foreign vessels are required to have in their service a United States or Canadian registered pilot.

(See 33 CFR 162.165 and 207.580 , chapter 2, for regulations.) Local harbor regulations are established by the Corporation Counsel and enforced by the harbormaster, who may be reached at City Hall.

notes.quote: The Vessel Operation Restriction Regulations provide a speed limit of 8 km/h (4.3 knots) on Chenail Ecarté and Sydenham River as far as Dresden, which is 10 miles east of Wallaceburg.
This speed limit reduces wake damage to dykes and low farmland.
The current in Chenail Ecarté sets east and south from St. Clair River to Lake St. Clair.
Rates of up to 1.2 knots have been reported in Chenail Ecarté where it leaves St. Clair River.

The remaining waters of Lake Huron are Great Lakes undesignated waters; the above vessels are required to have in their service a United States or Canadian registered pilot or other officer qualified for Great Lakes undesignated waters.
